the physician has a moral obligation to refer patients with cancer to RCTs if the patients are eligible, and if the physician has a reasonable expectation that the patient's health interests will be served best by participation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the importance of the ethical obligation to contribute to the development of knowledge in medicine, as well as the importance of the obligation to the patient.
we need to do more research on the ethical issues surrounding the referral of patients with cancer to clinical trials.
we need to improve our ability to communicate with patients, to explain to them the nature of RCTs and to help them understand the potential risks and benefits of participation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the ethical obligations of referring physicians in the referral process, especially in the context of RCTs.
the ethical obligation to serve the health interest of the individual patient takes priority over the obligation to contribute to the advance of scientific knowledge.

the referring physician's role in the referral of patients to clinical trials is to ensure that the patient is fully informed and has a complete understanding of the nature and purpose of the trial, the patient's role in the trial, and the potential benefits and risks to the patient.
